questions.question: Using a hand-held mobile device while driving is:

options.text: Acceptable if weather conditions are clear.

questions.explanation: Using a hand-held mobile device while driving a commercial vehicle is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Air tank drains are used to:

options.text: Should not be used in cold weather.
Remove water and oil from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in brake systems contains water and oil. If not removed, this can damage the system. Air tanks have drain valves to remove water and oil from the compressed air.

questions.question: How can you tell if a converter dolly has anti-lock brakes?

options.text: The dolly has a sticker with the letters "ABS."
There is a plaque on the side of the dolly.
There is a yellow lamp on the left side of the dolly.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a yellow lamp on the left side of the dolly.
questions.explanation: Converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have anti-lock brakes. A yellow lamp on the left side of the dolly indicates the presence of anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: When traveling down a steep grade, switch into a lower gear:

options.text: After you have started the grade.
As far down the grade as possible.

questions.explanation: Shift into a low gear before starting a downhill grade. Gravity will increase your vehicle's speed when going downhill, so be prepared.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of fatigue?
questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include difficulty focusing, frequent blinking, heavy eyelids, yawning, rubbing eyes, daydreaming, trouble remembering the last few miles driven, missing exits or signs, trouble keeping your head up, drifting from your lane, following too closely, hitting rumble strips, and feeling restless or irritable.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, stopping distance:

options.text: Is longer than on a regular driving surface.
Is shorter than on a regular driving surface.
Is about the same as on a regular driving surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is longer than on a regular driving surface.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance increases on slippery surfaces because there is less traction available.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of driver fatigue?
questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include difficulty focusing, frequent blinking, heavy eyelids, yawning, rubbing eyes, daydreaming, wandering thoughts, trouble remembering the last few miles, missing exits or signs, trouble keeping your head up, drifting from your lane, following too closely, hitting rumble strips, and feeling restless or irritable.

questions.question: ABS brakes:

options.text: Prevent your vehicle from accelerating uphill.

questions.explanation: Anti-lock brakes prevent a vehicle's wheels from locking up when the driver brakes hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: When checking your vehicle before a trip, look under it to:

options.text: See if the vehicle is on an incline.
Check for fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
See if the vehicle is in a parking spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
questions.explanation: When checking your vehicle, look under it for fresh leaks of oil, grease, or fuel. Also check around the vehicle for hazards like other vehicles, people, or low-hanging wires or branches.

questions.question: Skids caused by over-acceleration can usually be fixed by:

options.text: Removing your foot from the accelerator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Removing your foot from the accelerator.
questions.explanation: Remove your foot from the accelerator to fix a skid caused by over-acceleration. This type of skid happens most often on snow or ice.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, you should check for all of the following, except:

options.text: Tires with too much air pressure.
Tires that are worn down too much.

questions.explanation: When checking your tires, make sure they have at least 4/32 inch of tread depth in the front and at least 2/32 inch in the back. Check that tires are not worn, cracked, or over-inflated, and that all tires are the same size.

questions.question: Which gas would be a problem if the exhaust system is broken?
questions.explanation: A leaking exhaust system can let carbon monoxide, which is poisonous, enter the cab or sleeper area.

questions.question: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air supply leaks from the air brake system:

options.text: The trailer will have no brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will have no brakes.
questions.explanation: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air tank leaks and loses all air pressure, the brakes will not work and the wheels will spin freely.

questions.question: On flat surfaces, wheel chocks:

options.text: Can stop a parked vehicle from rolling.
Make it easier for a parked vehicle to roll.
Should only be used on the front driver's side tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can stop a parked vehicle from rolling.
questions.explanation: When you cannot use the parking brake, wheel chocks can be placed to hold a parked vehicle in place on a flat surface.

questions.question: How many hours of sleep do adults need each day to stay alert?
questions.explanation: Getting enough rest is important for safe driving. Most people need eight to nine hours of sleep each night to stay alert.

questions.question: A safety valve opens at ____ pounds per square inch (psi).
questions.explanation: The safety valve protects air tanks and the air brake system from too much air pressure. It is set to open at 150 psi.

questions.question: When stopping, you should press the brake pedal by:
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal down slowly and smoothly. Gradual braking helps you keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not apply brakes if the vehicle is in neutral.

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park. You can also use wheel chocks if needed.

questions.question: People working on a broken-down vehicle:

options.text: May be focused on the repair and not notice traffic nearby.
Do not have to follow traffic laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be focused on the repair and not notice traffic nearby.
questions.explanation: When driving near people who are fixing a broken-down vehicle on the roadside, be careful. They are focused on the repair and may not see your vehicle coming.

questions.question: Broken suspension parts:

options.text: Should be fixed, but not right away.

questions.explanation: The suspension system supports the vehicle and load while keeping the axles in place. A broken suspension is very dangerous and must be repaired immediately.
